messages:
Alex M: Heads up — EU-west cluster showing a weird drain/backpressure pattern that leaves a ton of small-GPU pods scattered. Nodes end up with 0.25–0.5 GPU free, we then get lots of preempt evictions and noisy reschedules. Not a full fragmentation wave but steady waste.
Priya R: saw that too. started ~09:22UTC? autoscaler scaled down a few racks and a bunch of best-effort pods stayed pinned due to node-affinity.
Jamie C: any network errors around the same time? the scheduler logs showed repeated BindTimeouts then evictions.
Alex M: attaching short log excerpt: ```
I0319 09:22:14.123 scheduler.go:456] FailedBinding: pod gpu-train-12 -> binding timeout to node gpunode-7 
I0319 09:22:14.130 eviction.go:78] Evicting pod gpu-train-12 due to failed binding/backpressure
```
Sam K: infra-bot posted scale down event at 09:21:58 to be exact. I think scale-down + taints-for-drain is colliding with our gang-affinity for training jobs.
Marta S: I can repro on a staging rack. It looks like taint "ephemeral-drain=true:NoSchedule" lands, the preemptor picks up lower-QoS pods but they have nodeAffinity that requires some gpu-labels which only exist on those partially freed nodes. Scheduler rejects then preempts elsewhere causing more fragmentation.
Leo T: interesting — this smells like our preemption threshold + topology weight interaction. If topologyWeight prefers spreading for GPU labels we avoid co-locating leftovers, leaving lots of <1 GPU holes.
Priya R: can we temporarily lower topologySpread weight or increase binpackScore for gpu resources? That might let the scheduler consolidate.
Alex M: yes, quick mitigation suggestion: bump nodeScoring prioritizer weight for binpack (gpu) from 30 -> 60 and set preemptionThreshold to 0.7. Shall I try a canary?
Sam K: +1 for canary in eu-west1-rack-b. Also run a one-off descheduler pass to evict tiny best-effort pods that are blocking compacting.
Marta S: descheduler plan: run policy that removes pod-affinity/anti-affinity constraints for BE pods older than 1h and forces reschedule. Will queue a job.
infra-bot: [autoscaler] scaledown: rack-b-3 removed at 2026-03-19T09:21:58Z — reason: low utilization.
Jamie C: low-risk route: canary change scheduler config on a single scheduler instance -> observe placement score deltas in the console for 30m. If good, roll to cluster. We should also track GPU-utilization tail latency.
Leo T: I'll prepare the scheduler config diff and include metric alerts: "small_free_gpu_slots > 25%" and "eviction_rate > 1/min". Also add temporary fast-fallback to avoid preempt churn (cooldown 3m).
Alex M: after canary we'll follow with a descheduler run; if that doesn't reclaim contiguous 1.0 GPU blocks we may need to tweak taint timing (delay taint application by 2m) so drain doesn't rip the packing apart.
Priya R: timeline?
Sam K: aiming to patch canary at 09:40 UTC, monitor 9:40–10:10, descheduler at 10:15 if safe. I'll own rollout and rollback.
Marta S: I'll run repro in staging with identical autoscaler events to validate.
Jamie C: one more action: add a short-term cost tracker to surface the extra GPU-hours being consumed due to these holes. Want a $/hr delta in the rollout dashboard.
Alex M: sounds good. I'll create the scheduler PR and link here. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
Leo T: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/scheduler/compare/pack-score-canary — contains weight bump + cooldown.
Priya R: watching logs, ping me if evictions spike.
Sam K: rolling canary now.
Alex M: closing loop — canary stable at +25% consolidation, eviction rate down to baseline. Descheduler run postponed. Will follow up with postmortem if any regressions.
